policies.title: British citizens: right of abode and home access
policies.summary: British citizens have the statutory right of abode and are outside the foreign visitor permission requirement.
conditions: The catalog's GB code cannot distinguish British Citizen passports from other British-national document statuses; this citizenship policy is limited to British citizens and must not be read as a finding about every UK-issued passport.
The ETA guidance separately says British citizens do not need an ETA.
The right of abode evidence does not determine carrier-document checks or treatment under a different passport used by a dual national.

policies.title: Irish citizens: Common Travel Area permission exemption
policies.summary: Irish citizens do not require leave to enter or remain in the United Kingdom, subject to statutory exceptions.
conditions: This is a citizenship/status rule for Irish citizens, not a rule for all travellers departing from Ireland or travelling on an Irish-issued document.
Section 3ZA exceptions apply where the Irish citizen is subject to a deportation order, an exclusion decision, or a specified international travel ban.
The ETA guidance says Irish citizens do not need an ETA; non-British and non-Irish family members are not covered merely through the CTA relationship.

policies.title: ETA-national ordinary passports: phased pre-2025 rollout cohorts
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require an ETA before travel to the UK from their respective stated rollout dates when seeking a visitor entry of up to six months.
conditions: QA has been subject to the ETA requirement for travel on or after 2023-11-15; BH, KW, OM, AE and SA for travel on or after 2024-02-22.
An ETA is required in advance of travel but does not itself grant permission to enter; the traveller seeks permission on arrival.

An otherwise listed national does not need an ETA if they hold valid UK entry clearance or permission to enter or stay; British Overseas Territory Citizens and British Nationals (Overseas) are also ETA-exempt by document/status.
A listed national lawfully resident in Ireland and travelling to the UK from elsewhere in the CTA is ETA-exempt, with evidence of lawful Irish residence required on request from age 16.
The ETA rule includes a Visitor other than a Marriage/Civil Partnership Visitor for stays up to six months; a different purpose or longer visit may require a visa.
Transit is not flattened into this visitor policy: an ETA is needed when passing UK border control, while airside transit has separate rules.

application.label: UK ETA official application
steps: Confirm that the passport nationality, travel date, purpose and any exception make an ETA appropriate.
Apply online or in the UK ETA app using the passport that will be used for travel.
Provide the required email address, passport and facial image, and pay the fee.
Travel only with the passport linked to the granted ETA; entry permission is decided on arrival.

policies.title: ETA-national ordinary passports: 8 January 2025 rollout cohort
policies.summary: The listed nationalities require an ETA for UK short visitor travel on or after 8 January 2025, subject to the stated document and status exceptions.
conditions: TW is within this policy only where the Taiwan passport includes the identification-card number issued by the competent Taiwan authority; otherwise the visa-national rule applies.
HK is limited to a Hong Kong SAR passport and MO to a Macao SAR passport under the Visa National List exceptions; the underlying PRC nationality alone does not create this route.

An otherwise listed national does not need an ETA if they hold valid UK entry clearance or permission to enter or stay; British Overseas Territory Citizens and British Nationals (Overseas) are ETA-exempt by document/status.
A listed national lawfully resident in Ireland and travelling from elsewhere in the CTA does not need an ETA, subject to the Immigration Rules residence definition and evidence condition.
The rule is for a Visitor other than a Marriage/Civil Partnership Visitor for up to six months; an ETA is valid for two years or until the linked passport expires, whichever is sooner.
Airside transit is outside this visitor classification; passing UK border control requires an ETA for an ETA national.

application.label: UK ETA official application
steps: Check the passport-specific Taiwan, Hong Kong or Macao condition where applicable, plus any ETA exemption.
Apply online or in the UK ETA app using the passport for travel.
Provide the required email address, passport and facial image, and pay the fee.
Use the linked passport for travel after grant; an ETA does not guarantee admission.

policies.title: ETA-national ordinary passports: 2 April 2025 European rollout cohort
policies.summary: The listed European and microstate nationalities require an ETA for UK short visitor travel on or after 2 April 2025, subject to stated exceptions.
conditions: This policy does not include Irish citizens, who have a separate statutory leave exemption.
The VA code represents the nationality list's Vatican City entry; the Visa National List separately exempts Holy See service, temporary service and diplomatic passports from its visa-national rule.

A listed national with valid UK entry clearance or permission to enter or stay does not need an ETA; ETA-exempt British document statuses and the lawful-Ireland-resident CTA exception remain applicable.
The ETA route is for a Visitor other than a Marriage/Civil Partnership Visitor staying up to six months; approval authorises travel, not entry.
Airside transit has separate rules; an ETA national passing UK border control needs an ETA.

application.label: UK ETA official application
steps: Confirm the trip is within ETA visitor scope and that no exception applies.
Apply online or in the UK ETA app with the passport to be used for travel.
Submit the required passport, facial image, email address and fee.
Travel using that passport only after grant; entry remains a border decision.

policies.title: Visa-national ordinary passports: advance UK visitor entry clearance
policies.summary: The listed nationals require entry clearance in advance for a UK visit or another purpose of less than six months, except for the specified document, school-party and temporary transitional exceptions.
conditions: The list is expressly subject to exceptions and is not an airside-transit determination; transit rules depend on whether the traveller passes UK border control.
CN is visa-national except where a PRC national holds an HKSAR or Macao SAR passport; those two document-specific routes are modelled as HK and MO ETA policies.
TW is visa-national except where the passport includes the Taiwan identification-card number; that qualifying document is an ETA national, as modelled separately.
The Holy See service, temporary service and diplomatic passport exception does not establish treatment of every VA document; the ordinary Vatican City ETA route is modelled separately.
All non-national-passport documents and stateless persons are visa-national unless a stated exception applies; those document classes are outside this ordinary-passport catalog.

The rules contain limited France and Germany organised-school-party exceptions and a time-limited 2026 Nicaragua/St Lucia ETA transitional exception; neither is a general ordinary-passport entitlement.
Marriage/civil-partnership visit or notice, and a visit over six months, are outside the cited visa-list exceptions and may require entry clearance even where an exception otherwise applies.

application.label: UK Standard Visitor visa official application guidance
steps: Confirm that no listed document-specific or temporary exception applies and select the appropriate visitor route.
Apply online before travelling to the UK.
Attend the required visa application-centre appointment.
Travel only after the required entry clearance is granted.
